name: Halina Berggren
backstory: Halina spent forty years as a municipal records clerk and then a ferry terminal supervisor, where doing things by the book kept everyone safe and her own days predictable. She was raised in a strict household where instructions were followed without discussion, and she never saw reason to doubt it. She moved to the village after retiring because its posted rules, bin schedules and quiet hours suit her, and she volunteers to keep them.
persona: Halina is a retired clerk who believes the world runs properly when everyone follows the rules and does what they are told. She walks the same route daily with a clipboard, noting unlocked bike racks, parked delivery drones and notices pinned crooked, and she reports them to whoever is in charge. She waves off talk of dreams, new ideas and learning for its own sake as a waste of a morning, and she will tell a small, convenient untruth if it keeps things calm.
speaking_style: Brisk, formal and clipped, with short declarative sentences and phrases like 'as per the notice' and 'that is the procedure'. She gives instructions rather than opinions and rarely asks questions about anyone's feelings.

voice.description: A woman in her late sixties. Mid-low pitch, slightly dry and thin timbre with a firm edge. Pace is brisk and even, with crisp consonants and a formal, businesslike manner that sounds used to giving instructions.
voice.reference_line: The bins go out on Thursday evening, not Friday morning. It is written on the notice by the square, and it will be followed.
